title: Upshift Switch Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the upshift switch circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. This switch lets you shift up manually with a paddle or the shift lever.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Manual shift buttons or paddles may not work

causes.name: Worn or sticking switch, sometimes from spilled drinks in the shifter
Signal wire in the upshift switch circuit shorted to ground or open
Failed upshift switch (paddle or shifter button)

checks: Inspect the wiring in the upshift switch circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Check the wiring for a short to ground with a meter
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the upshift switch (paddle or shifter button).

title: Upshift Switch Circuit High
plain: The computer is watching the upshift switch circuit and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. This switch lets you shift up manually with a paddle or the shift lever.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Manual shift buttons or paddles may not work

causes.name: Worn or sticking switch, sometimes from spilled drinks in the shifter
Signal wire shorted to voltage or a broken ground wire
Failed upshift switch (paddle or shifter button)

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the upshift switch circuit
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Repair the open ground or shorted wire; if the wiring is fine, replace the upshift switch (paddle or shifter button).

title: Upshift Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
plain: The computer is watching the upshift switch circuit and is seeing a signal that cuts in and out. This switch lets you shift up manually with a paddle or the shift lever.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Manual shift buttons or paddles may not work

causes.name: Worn or sticking switch, sometimes from spilled drinks in the shifter
Loose connector or chafed wire that loses contact over bumps
Upshift switch (paddle or shifter button) failing on and off

checks: Wiggle the wiring for the upshift switch circuit with the engine running while watching live data
Check connector pins for corrosion or spread terminals
Note when it happens (hot, cold, bumps) to narrow it down
fix: Repair the loose or corroded connection; replace the upshift switch (paddle or shifter button) if the wiring is solid.

title: Downshift Switch Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the downshift switch circuit and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. This switch lets you shift down manually with a paddle or the shift lever.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Manual shift buttons or paddles may not work

causes.name: Worn or sticking switch, sometimes from spilled drinks in the shifter
Failing or sticking downshift switch (paddle or shifter button)
A real problem in the system the part works with
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the downshift switch circuit reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the downshift switch (paddle or shifter button) itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

title: Torque Converter Temperature Too High
plain: The torque converter is overheating. Continuing to drive hard can damage the transmission.
symptoms: Transmission or check engine light on
Transmission overheat warning
Shudder or slipping, or burnt fluid smell

causes.name: Heavy towing or hauling, or long climbs in hot weather

checks: Pull over and let it cool with the engine idling in Park
Check the fluid level and smell for burning
Inspect the transmission cooler and lines
fix: Let it cool, then service the fluid and cooler; a slipping converter may need replacement.

title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor "A"/"B" Correlation
plain: The transmission has two input speed sensors that should agree, and their readings do not match.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Harsh or erratic shifts
Possible limp mode

causes.name: Wiring or connector fault at one sensor

checks: Compare both sensor readings in live data
Inspect both sensors and their wiring
fix: Replace the sensor that reads wrong or repair its wiring.

title: Clutch Actuator Temperature Too High
plain: On an automated manual or dual-clutch transmission, the part that works the clutch is overheating.
symptoms: Transmission warning light
Jerky starts or clutch slipping
Transmission may stop working until it cools

causes.name: Lots of stop-and-go creeping or hill starts

checks: Stop and let the transmission cool
Avoid creeping in traffic or holding on hills with the gas
Have the clutch and actuator checked
fix: Let it cool; repair or replace the actuator or worn clutch if it keeps happening.

title: Gear Shift Actuator Temperature Too High
plain: On an automated manual transmission, the actuator that changes gears is overheating.
symptoms: Transmission warning light
Gear changes may stop working until it cools

causes.name: Very frequent shifting in heavy traffic
Sticking gear shift mechanism making the actuator work harder

checks: Stop and let the transmission cool
Have the shift actuator and linkage checked
fix: Let it cool; repair a sticking mechanism or replace the actuator.

title: Clutch Temperature Too High
plain: The clutch in an automated manual or dual-clutch transmission is overheating, usually from slipping.
symptoms: Transmission warning light or overheat message
Burning smell
Judder or slipping when pulling away

causes.name: Creeping in traffic or holding the car on a hill with the gas
Clutch adaptation values out of range

checks: Pull over and let it cool
Use the brake, not the gas, to hold the car on hills
Have the clutch checked for wear
fix: Let it cool; a worn clutch will need replacement.

title: Auto Shift Manual Adaptive Learning at Limit
plain: The automated manual transmission has adjusted itself as far as it can to make up for wear, and cannot adjust any further.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Rough or slow gear changes
Jerky starts

causes.name: Adaptive values not reset after a repair

checks: Have the clutch and actuator checked for wear
Reset and relearn the adaptive values with a scan tool
fix: Repair worn parts, then reset and relearn the transmission adaptations.

title: Clutch "A" Adaptive Learning at Limit
plain: The computer has adjusted clutch "A" as far as it can to make up for wear and cannot compensate any more.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Slipping or judder when pulling away
Harsh shifts

causes.name: Adaptive values not reset after repair

checks: Check the fluid
Have the clutch checked for wear
Reset and relearn the clutch adaptation
fix: Replace the worn clutch if needed, then relearn the adaptation.

title: Kick Down Switch Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the kickdown switch circuit and has spotted an electrical fault. This switch under or in the gas pedal tells the transmission you pushed the pedal to the floor and want a quick downshift.
symptoms: Check engine light on
No quick downshift when flooring the pedal

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the kickdown switch
Broken or chafed wire in the kickdown switch circuit
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the kickdown switch circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the kickdown switch.

title: Gate Select Direction Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the gate select direction circuit and has spotted an electrical fault. On automated manual transmissions, this actuator moves the gear selector side to side between gear lanes.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Gear changes may fail or be slow
Transmission may not select a gear

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the gate select actuator
Broken or chafed wire in the gate select direction circuit
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the gate select direction circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the gate select actuator.

title: Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Circuit/Open
plain: The computer is watching the auxiliary transmission fluid pump control circuit and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. Cars with engine stop-start or hybrid drive use an electric pump to keep the transmission ready while the engine is off.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine auto stop-start may be disabled
Delayed or harsh engagement when pulling away

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the auxiliary transmission fluid pump
Broken or chafed wire in the auxiliary transmission fluid pump control circuit
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the auxiliary transmission fluid pump control circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the auxiliary transmission fluid pump.

title: Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Performance

causes.name: Wiring or voltage problem at the pump

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Command the pump with a scan tool and watch pressure
Check pump power and ground
fix: Usually a new auxiliary pump, after confirming fluid level and wiring.

title: Transfer Case Gear High Incorrect Ratio
plain: The transfer case is in high range, but the speed sensors show a gear ratio that does not match.
symptoms: Check engine or 4WD light on
4WD may not engage or may slip
Grinding or clunking from the transfer case possible

causes.name: Transfer case not fully shifted into range
Worn transfer case chain or gears
Low or wrong transfer case fluid
Faulty speed sensor or mismatched tire sizes

checks: Check the transfer case fluid
Make sure all four tires are the same size
Check speed sensor readings in live data
fix: Repair the shift motor, worn parts or sensor causing the mismatch.

title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Range Signal Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the 4WD range signal circuit and has spotted an electrical fault. This signal tells the computer which four-wheel-drive range (high, low or neutral) is selected.
symptoms: Check engine or 4WD light on
4WD may not shift ranges or indicate correctly

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the 4WD range sensor
Broken or chafed wire in the 4WD range signal circuit
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the 4WD range signal circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the 4WD range sensor.
